SHANGHAI, 22nd November 1940.

To the Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai Municipal Police,
Shanghai.

Dear Sir:-

The receipt of your letter dated November 20,
1940, is acknowledged with thanks, and contents have
been noted.

Nevertheless, I would like to point out
again that the first Press notice regarding the per-
formance of "DIE MASKEN FALLEN" at the hall of the
British Embassy on November 9th and 10th appeared in
the "Jewish Chronicle" on October 20th, 1940, already,
but I was not approached nor informed that the Police
were against the production.

In this connection, I have heard rumours that
it is intended to produce the play in English in the
Lyceum Theatre. I do not know, at present, if these ru-
mours are based on truth. I would appreciate if you
would inform me whether you know of this matter and what
attitude you will take towards the production in English
and presumably played by English actors.

Regarding a close co-operation, I am recalling
a telephone conversation with Mr. Young sometime ago,
during which it was tentatively agreed that we would con-
sult one another before further licences for German lan-
guage papers were granted. Nevertheless, a licence to the
"MITARBEITER" was granted without such consultation, and
we only heard by chance of the establishment of a further
paper the first issue of which is, to our knowledge, to
appear today.

Whilst no objection is raised by this Committee
to the "MITARBEITER", it must nevertheless be realized by
you that co-operation on our part is made somewhat diffi-
cult in the circumstances.

Yours faithfully,
“I.C.” ORGANIZATION
FOR
IMMIGRANTS
Hon. Secretary.

上海。

尊敬的先生：-

谨此确认收到您1940年11月20日的来信，并感谢之，内容已悉。

然而，我想再次指出，关于11月9日和10日在英国大使馆大厅演出《面具卸下》（"DIE MASKEN FALLEN"）的第一则新闻公告，早已于1940年10月20日刊登在《犹太纪事报》（"Jewish Chronicle"）上，但当时并未有人接洽我，也未通知我警方反对此次演出。

就此而言，我听到谣言称该剧打算在兰心大戏院（Lyceum Theatre）以英文演出。目前我不知道这些谣言是否属实。如果您知晓此事，以及您对这场 presumably 由英国演员演出的英文剧目持何种态度，恳请告知。

关于密切合作一事，我回想起不久前与杨先生（Mr. Young）的一次电话交谈，期间我们暂定在颁发更多德语报刊许可证之前相互协商。然而，《同事报》（"MITARBEITER"）的许可证未经此类协商即获颁发，而我们只是偶然得知又有一家新报刊成立，据我们所知，其首期将于今日出版。

虽然本委员会对《同事报》并无异议，但您必须认识到，在这种情况下，我方进行合作变得有些困难。

此致，
敬礼

I am convinced it is in the public interest to

THE INTERNATIONAL COMMITTEE FOR THE
ORGANIZATION OF EUROPEAN IMMIGRANTS
IN CHINA

SHANGHAI, 19th November 1940.

To the Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai Municipal Police,
Shanghai.

Dear Sir,

In connection with the recent production of the
play "DIE MASKEN FALLEN" I had the pleasure yesterday of
a call from Sub-Inspector Wittinsky who suggested that in
matters of Public Interest wherein the Emigrants in our
midst might possibly be concerned or their special interests
may be affected, there should be more co-operation between
the S.M.P. and this organization.

May I observe that I am not aware that such co-
operation has been lacking on the part of this Committee
which has, indeed, given all the assistance that it could
reasonably give in the past and certainly intends to do
so also in the future.

With reference to this special case, may I be
permitted to observe that evidently the Police were ac-
quainted with the play and the intention to produce it
quite sometime ago.

Furthermore, the "Shanghai Jewish Chronicle"
brought press-notices beginning with its issue of 20th
October almost daily, the "North China Daily News" also
printed an article in this connection on the 31st October.

As far as this Committee is aware, not until then
was any objection raised to the production of the play.
There was, therefore, no previous occasion whatsoever for
this organization to take any steps in the direction of
persuading the producers to abstain from their project.

The producers had, themselves, gone so far with
their project at the time when Mr. Speelman's letter ap-
peared in the "North China Daily News" that, evidently,
they could not cancel the performances without taking a
considerable loss.

I myself attached no special significance to
the production of the play although, in private conver-
sation, I voiced doubts as to the advisability or desire-
ability of producing it here and at this time, even going
so far as to say, that I thought the production illtimed,
but I cannot claim that my own opinion must be conclusive
and correct nor have I any means or wish to impose such
opinion on any one. I must add that the play was not sub-
mitted to me for reading and I have no knowledge of its con-
tents beyond that which has appeared in the Press subsequent
to its initial production.

上海，1940年11月19日。

致上海公共租界工部局警务处处长，
上海。

尊敬的先生，

关于最近上演的戏剧《面具卸下》（"DIE MASKEN FALLEN"），我昨日荣幸地接待了维廷斯基副督察（Sub-Inspector Wittinsky）的来访，他建议在上海公共租界工部局警务处与本组织之间，就涉及公众利益、可能关乎我们要中间的移民或其特殊利益受影响的事项上，应加强合作。

请允许我指出，我并不认为本委员会缺乏此类合作，事实上，本委员会在过去已提供了所有合理范围内能提供的协助，并肯定打算在未来继续如此。

关于这一特定案例，请允许我指出，显然警方在相当早之前就已知晓该剧及上演意图。

此外，《上海犹太纪事报》（"Shanghai Jewish Chronicle"）从10月20日的那一期开始几乎每天都刊登相关新闻公告，《字林西报》（"North China Daily News"）也于10月31日刊登了一篇相关文章。

据本委员会所知，直到那时才有人对该剧的上演提出异议。因此，本组织此前没有任何机会采取任何步骤去劝说制作人放弃其计划。

当斯佩尔曼先生（Mr. Speelman）的信在《字林西报》上发表时，制作人自己的项目已经推进到如此地步，显然，他们若不取消演出就会遭受相当大的损失。

我个人并未对该剧的上演赋予特殊意义，尽管在私下谈话中，我曾对此时此地演出该剧的明智性或可取性表示怀疑，甚至直言我认为上演时机不当，但我不能声称我的意见必须是决定性和正确的，我也没有任何手段或愿望将这种意见强加给任何人。我必须补充说明，该剧并未提交给我阅读，除了初次演出后见诸报端的内容外，我对该剧内容一无所知。

“I. C.” to the Commissioner of Police, S.M.P., Shanghai.

The fact is, that not until Friday last was I approached
with the request that I use the influence of my organization to
have further performances, which were advertised to take place on
the 16th and 17th inst., cancelled and the "I.C." did what it
could, in the very short space of time at its disposal, in this
direction.

Had the "I.C." been approached by the S.M.P. in the first
place with the request that it use its good offices, it might
have been possible to persuade the producers in a friendly way
to comply with the, no doubt well grounded, wishes of the Police.

I can give you the assurance that this Committee is always
ready to co-operate, as far as it is in its power to do so, with
the authorities but, reasonably, it must be given a fair chance
to do so or, otherwise, a situation might arise which it is im-
possible to remedy and which might possibly do harm, more especi-
ally to the Emigrants themselves.

Yours faithfully,
“I.C.” ORGANIZATION
FOR
EMIGRANTS
[Signature]

“国际委员会”致上海公共租界工部局警务处处长。

事实是，直到上周五，我才接到请求，希望我利用本组织的影响力取消原定于本月16日和17日举行的后续演出，“国际委员会”在极短的时间内尽其所能做了这方面的工作。

如果上海公共租界工部局警务处起初就接洽“国际委员会”，请求其从中斡旋，或许有可能以友好的方式说服制作人遵从警方无疑有充分理由的愿望。

我可以向您保证，本委员会随时准备在力所能及的范围内与当局合作，但合理地讲，必须给予其公平的机会这样做，否则，可能会出现无法补救的局面，并可能造成损害，尤其是对移民自身造成损害。

此致，
敬礼

Emigre Showing
Of Jewish Play
Cancelled Here

German Pressure Said
Brought To Bear On
Local Committee

Fear that Jews in Germany
would suffer further persecution
caused sponsors of "The Mask
Fall," a locally-written play in
German by Jewish emigres, to
cancel further performances, it
was learned today.

The play was not performed on
Saturday and Sunday evenings as
had been scheduled, although two
performances were held during
the previous week at the British
Press Attache's Hall on The Bund.
Two additional showings for the
coming Saturday and Sunday
have also been cancelled.

"Illness" Said Reason

The Jewish emigre committee
declared that the reason for the
failure of the show to take place
on Saturday and last night was
due to "the illness of one of the
principal actors."

It is learned, however that a
member of the German Consulate
in Shanghai telephoned to Mr.
Paul Komor of the Jewish emigre
committee and "requested" that
further performances of the play
should be cancelled.

Reprisals Against Jews

The German official, it is under-
stood, also indicated that unless
the play would be stopped reprisals
would be taken against Jews liv-
ing in Germany and also against
Jewish emigres here.

Questioned this morning about
the telephone conversation with
the German official, Mr. Komor
declared to the Shanghai Evening
Post that he did not wish to deny
or confirm it, adding that he was
not the press spokesman for the
Jewish emigre committee, and that
it would be necessary to speak to
Mr. Ellis Hayim.

Mr. Ellis Hayim, Chairman of the
Jewish emigre committee, when
questioned by the Shanghai Even-
ing Post, would not deny that a
German official had spoken to Mr.
Komor, but declared that he him-
self had received no communication
from any German source.

"The Mask Fall" written by
Hans Neumann and produced un-
der the auspices of the Jewish Emi-
gre Committee in Austria following the Nazi
occupation. A translation from the
German has recently been prepared
into English by Julius Klein and
is being presented here in the original
German.

Prior to the two first performan-
ces of the play which were
held last week, strong objections
were raised against the play by the
German Consul who claimed it
was anti-German propaganda and
that its performance would result
in reprisals against Jews in Germany.
page_data.zh:
犹太剧目
在此取消
演出

称德国方面
向当地委员会
施加压力

据悉，由于担心在德国的犹太人遭受进一步迫害，《面具落下》（The Mask Fall）——一部由犹太流亡者用德语在当地创作的剧本——的赞助人取消了后续演出。

尽管上周在外滩英国新闻专员礼堂举行了两场演出，但该剧并未按计划在周六和周日晚上上演。原定于下周六和周日举行的另外两场演出也已取消。

称“生病”为理由

犹太流亡者委员会宣称，演出未能在周六和昨晚举行的原因是“主要演员之一生病”。

然而据了解，上海德国领事馆的一名成员致电犹太流亡者委员会的 Paul Komor 先生，“要求”取消该剧的后续演出。

对犹太人的报复

据了解，这位德国官员还暗示，除非停止该剧的演出，否则将对居住在德国的犹太人以及此地的犹太流亡者进行报复。

今早被问及与德国官员的电话交谈时，Komor 先生向《上海晚邮报》（Shanghai Evening Post）表示，他既不愿否认也不愿证实此事，并补充说他不是犹太流亡者委员会的新闻发言人，有必要去询问 Ellis Hayim 先生。

犹太流亡者委员会主席 Ellis Hayim 先生在接受《上海晚邮报》询问时，并未否认德国官员曾与 Komor 先生交谈，但他声称自己未收到来自任何德国方面的信件。

《面具落下》由 Hans Neumann 编剧，在纳粹占领奥地利后，由犹太流亡者委员会在奥地利支持下制作。Julius Klein 最近将其从德语翻译成英文，但此处演出仍使用德语原版。

在该剧上周举行首两场演出之前，德国总领事对该剧提出了强烈反对，声称这是反德宣传，其演出将导致对德国境内犹太人的报复。

30名演职人员均为犹太流亡者，其中包括几位在维也纳拥有多年舞台经验的演员。领衔主演的是著名的夜总会艺人 Lilly Fuhr 小姐。

page_data.en:
Jewish Play Is
Outstanding Hit

Money Repaid As SMP
Appear On Scene;
JRC Objects

Despite several attempts by the
Jewish Refugee Committee here to
prevent its showing, "The Masks
Fall," an original five-act play by
Mark Siegelberg and Hans Wiener
on the persecution of Jews by the
Nazis, was presented to a capacity
audience in the British Press At-
tache's Hall on Saturday even-
ing.
Threats that the actors in the
play would not be given further
support by the committee if they
would perform, are understood to
have been made, while a final
effort on Saturday evening to
prevent the show from taking
place by obtaining police refusal
to allow any paying admission be-
cause of the nature of the play
was foiled when the sponsors of
the show refunded the money to
all those with tickets and allowed
them to retain their seats.
Outstanding Success
The play was an outstanding
success and by noteworthy and re-
strained portrayals on the part
of the cast, remained fine enter-
tainment, although obviously in-
tended to be propaganda.
Skilful portrayals were given in
the leading roles by Karl Bodan,
Lily Flohr, Helga Berliner (a
talented young lady, only 10 years
old), Fritz Melchior, Herbert
Zernik, Kurt Lewin, Ursula Perl-
hoefer and Josef Meister, while
those in the smaller parts, includ-
ed: Fritz Waechter, Heinz Gunther
and Margot Walloch.
The story is laid in Austria, a
few days before the Anschluss. It
develops a strong theme in which
an Aryan woman, married to a
Jewish newspaperman for 10 years,
seeks a divorce from her husband
because she has fallen in love
with another man. Before she can
get her divorce, however, her hus-
band and his old father are taken
away to a concentration camp
following the arrival of the Nazis.
Personal Effects
The tragic plight of her husband
brings a change to the woman who
decides to forget about the divorce
and, instead, applies every means
she can to obtain the release of
her husband and father-in-law.
This she finally succeeds in
doing, and obtains two tickets for
them to go to Shanghai. At the
station, the old father, terribly
shaken by the ordeal in the con-
centration camp, realizes that he
can still be free with his son's
other. He sacrifices his
freedom by throwing himself
before an on-coming train and
is killed leaving the couple
free to leave for Shanghai.
page_data.zh:
犹太剧目
大获成功

警务处介入后退款；
犹太难民委员会反对

尽管此地犹太难民委员会多次试图阻止演出，但由 Mark Siegelberg 和 Hans Wiener 创作的关于纳粹迫害犹太人的原创五幕剧《面具落下》，于周六晚上在英国新闻专员礼堂向满座观众演出。
据悉，有人威胁称，如果演员们坚持演出，委员会将不再给予支持；而在周六晚上，赞助方通过向所有持票人退款并允许他们保留座位，挫败了最后试图以该剧性质为由促使警方拒绝任何付费入场从而阻止演出的努力。
杰出成功
该剧取得了巨大成功，尽管明显意在宣传，但凭借演员们值得注意且克制的表演，仍不失为一场精彩的娱乐演出。
Karl Bodan、Lily Flohr、Helga Berliner（一位年仅10岁的才华横溢的小女孩）、Fritz Melchior、Herbert Zernik、Kurt Lewin、Ursula Perlhoefer 和 Josef Meister 在主要角色中展现了精湛的演技，而配角则包括：Fritz Waechter、Heinz Gunther 和 Margot Walloch。
故事背景设定在德奥合并前几天的奥地利。剧情展开一个强烈的主题：一位与犹太报业人士结婚10年的雅利安女子，因爱上另一名男子而寻求与丈夫离婚。然而，在她获得离婚之前，随着纳粹的到来，她的丈夫和年迈的父亲被带走送往集中营。
个人物品
丈夫的悲惨处境使这名女子发生了转变，她决定放弃离婚念头，转而竭尽所能设法释放丈夫和公公。
她最终成功了，并为他们弄到了两张前往上海的车票。在车站，饱受集中营折磨的老父亲意识到，只要儿子和其他人在一起，他仍可获得自由。他牺牲了自己的自由，投身于迎面驶来的火车前身亡，从而使这对夫妇得以自由前往上海。

August 20, 1940

Attached Communication from Dr. Mark Siegelberg.

With reference to the attached communication
from Dr. Mark Siegelberg, dated 12-8-40, wherein Police
permission to stage a German play entitled "The
Matrimony of Dr. Brach" is sought, the following
particulars have been obtained:

Dr. Mark Siegelberg, born in Luzk, Russia, on
the 11-6-1895, emigrated in his early youth to Vienna,
Austria, where he became the editor of several political
newspapers. When Austria was annexed by the third
Reich, Dr. Siegelberg was arrested and subsequently sent
to several concentration camps in Austria and Germany.

Following his release from the concentration
camp he left for Shanghai, arriving here, accompanied
by his wife, on the 27-6-39 on board the s.s. "Conte
Biancamano". Dr. Siegelberg arrived here with a German
"J" passport, but failed to prolong this passport and
several months ago took out Russian Emigrants' papers.

Following his arrival here, Dr. Siegelberg,
wrote a book entitled "Jewish Prisoner No.13877", in the
German language, which was printed by the American
Press", 542 Avenue Joffre. In the said book, Dr. Siegel-
berg describes his experiences in the various concentra-
ion camps in Austria and Germany.

On the 15-8-40, Dr. Siegelberg registered a
weekly German language newspaper "Das Echo" (Reg.No.F.94)
but did not commence publication, as he, at that time,
received an offer from the "Jewish Chronicle", Hamilton
House, to become it's editor. Dr. Siegelberg holds the
latter position at present, and is residing at 41/3
Muirhead Road.

Several weeks ago Dr. Siegelberg approached
D.S.I. Wittinsky enquiring as to the advisability of
staging his play "The Matrimony of Dr. Brach" in

关于附上的 Mark Siegelberg 博士 dated 1940年8月12日的来信，信中请求警方许可上演一部名为《布拉赫博士的婚姻》（The Matrimony of Dr. Brach）的德国戏剧，现已获取以下详情：

Mark Siegelberg 博士，1895年6月11日出生于俄罗斯卢茨克（Luzk），幼年移居奥地利维也纳，在那里成为几家政治报纸的编辑。当奥地利被第三帝国吞并时，Siegelberg 博士被捕，随后被送往奥地利和德国的多个集中营。

从集中营获释后，他前往上海，与其妻子一同于1939年6月27日乘坐“比安卡马诺伯爵号”（s.s. "Conte Biancamano"）轮抵达此地。Siegelberg 博士持德国“J”类护照抵达，但未延长该护照有效期，并于数月前办理了俄国流亡者证件。

抵达此地后，Siegelberg 博士用德语写了一本名为《犹太囚犯第13877号》的书，由爱文义路（Avenue Joffre）542号“美联社”（American Press）印刷。在该书中，Siegelberg 博士描述了他在奥地利和德国各个集中营的经历。

1940年8月15日，Siegelberg 博士注册了一份德语周报《回声报》（Das Echo）（注册号 F.94），但未开始出版，因为当时他收到了哈密顿大楼（Hamilton House）《犹太纪事报》（Jewish Chronicle）聘请其担任编辑的邀约。Siegelberg 博士目前担任该职，居住于穆尔黑德路（Muirhead Road）41/3号。

几周前，Siegelberg 博士接触了副督察 Wittinsky，询问上演其剧目《布拉赫博士的婚姻》是否适宜，地点在

Shanghai. He was informed by the latter that before
staging the play, he would have to get Police permission
through the official channels. However, before sub-
mitting the manuscript to the Police, Dr. Siegelberg sent
a copy of the same to Captain Inatsuki of the Japanese
Naval Landing Party, who stated that there are no
objections from his point of view, and forwarded a
letter of consent to Dr. Siegelberg.

The subject of the above play is definitely
political and deals partly with the "Racial Theory".
Scenes in a concentration camp (Act 4) dealing with
atrocities and tortures of Jews are vividly described.
The play which cannot be classified as cultural or
recreational is likely to cause incidents and breach of
peace, if staged publicly and without Police protection.
Attached to this report are several exerts of the play
and their translations.

Enquiries reveal that Dr. Siegelberg's reason
for staging "The Matrimony of Dr. Brach" in Shanghai is,
of an entirely commercial nature, namely, to assist
the sale of the said play in the U.S.A. To push the
sale of his manuscript Dr. Siegelberg requires enthu-
siastic press reviews, which he is able to obtain, being
the chief editor of the "Jewish Chronicle".

Dr. Siegelberg proposes to stage this
play in the Kinchow Road Camp, 100 Kinchow Road; the
date to be fixed subject to the issue of a permit by
the Police. The performance is proposed to take
place on three consecutive evenings, and an attendance
of 300 persons is expected on each occasion. Dr.
Siegelberg wishes to stress the fact that the audience
will be composed exclusively of German Jewish Refugees,
and believes that consequently there will not be any
disturbances.

上海。后者告知他，在上演该剧之前，他必须通过官方渠道获得警务处的许可。然而，在将剧本提交给警务处之前，西格尔伯格博士（Dr. Siegelberg）将副本送交日本海军陆战队队长稻月（Inatsuki，音译）上尉，后者表示从他的角度来看没有异议，并向西格尔伯格博士转发了同意函。

上述剧本的主题明确具有政治性，部分涉及“种族理论”。剧中第四幕关于集中营的场景，生动描述了针对犹太人的暴行和酷刑。该剧不能被归类为文化或娱乐活动，如果公开上演且没有警务保护，可能会引发事件并破坏和平。本报告附有该剧的几段摘录及其译文。

经查询得知，西格尔伯格博士在上海上演《布拉赫博士的婚姻》（"The Matrimony of Dr. Brach"）的原因完全出于商业性质，即为了协助该剧在美国的销售。为了推动其手稿的销售，西格尔伯格博士需要热情的媒体评论，而作为《犹太纪事报》（"Jewish Chronicle"）的主编，他能够获得这些评论。

西格尔伯格博士提议在金州路难民营（Kinchow Road Camp，地址：金州路100号）上演该剧；具体日期视警务处签发许可证的情况而定。演出计划连续三个晚上进行，预计每场观众人数为300人。西格尔伯格博士希望强调，观众将完全由德籍犹太难民组成，并相信因此不会发生任何骚乱。

Shanghai, August 12, 1940

To the
Commissioner,
Shanghai Municipal Police.

Sir,
We beg leave to apply for the permission to stage
our play, "Die Ehe des Doktor Brach" (The Matrimony of Dr.
Brach) in the Kinchow Road Refugee Jewish Centre (Kinchow
Buehne). The play is in the German language.
The above-mentioned play treats a problem, that for
years has occupied the minds of the Jews in Europe: "Racial
Theory". Following are the contents of the play:
Shortly before the German occupation of Austria,
Dr. Brach, a Jewish journalist, is about to be divorced by
his wife Christine, an "Aryan". The reason for the divorce
is, that Christine has fallen in love with another man. When
the Germans take over, Dr. Brach is arrested and taken to
a Concentration Camp. This event makes his wife change her
mind. She resolves to give up the divorce and to hold out
until her husband will be freed. She fights untiringly for
the release and finally succeeds. In this fight lasting
many months, the couple again gets convinced, that they
belong to one another, so they emigrate together to Shanghai.
The play sets out to prove, that love between two
people, even if they seemingly belong to different races, is
stronger than any "Racial Theory". The play does not decide
itself for either race and centres on the fight of the "Aryan"
woman for her Jewish husband.
On account of the problem, of universal interest,
discussed in it, the play has already been accepted by the
"Oesterreichische Buehne" in New York, the foremost theatre
of German refugees. At the same time the play is translated
into English.

twenty years editor-in-chief of one of the biggest dailies

先生，
我们恳请批准我们在金州路犹太难民中心（金州舞台，Kinchow Buehne）上演我们的剧本《布拉赫博士的婚姻》（Die Ehe des Doktor Brach）。该剧为德语剧。
上述剧本探讨了一个多年来困扰欧洲犹太人的问题：“种族理论”。以下是剧本内容概要：
在德国占领奥地利前夕，犹太记者布拉赫博士即将与其“雅利安”妻子克里斯汀离婚。离婚的原因是克里斯汀爱上了另一个男人。当德国人接管后，布拉赫博士被捕并被送往集中营。这一事件使他的妻子改变了主意。她决定放弃离婚，并坚持等到丈夫获释。她不懈地为释放丈夫而斗争，并最终成功。在这场持续数月的斗争中，夫妇二人再次确信他们属于彼此，因此他们共同移民至上海。
该剧旨在证明，两个人之间的爱，即使他们看似属于不同种族，也比任何“种族理论”更强大。该剧本身不偏袒任何种族，重点在于这位“雅利安”女性为其犹太丈夫进行的斗争。
鉴于其中讨论的问题具有普遍兴趣，该剧已被纽约最重要的德籍难民剧院“奥地利舞台”（"Oesterreichische Buehne"）接受。同时，该剧也被翻译成英文。

“Die Masken Fallen”:
An Amazing Protest

Jewish Relief Committee published

state that that publication seems
to me one of the most amazing poli-

perienced in Shanghai. So far as I

        Several weeks ago Dr.Siegelberg approached
D.S.I. Wittinsky enquiring as to the advisability of
staging his play "The Matrimony of Dr.Brach" in
Shanghai. He was informed by the latter that before
staging the play, he would have to get Police permission
through the official channels. However, before submitting
the manuscript to the Police, Dr.Siegelberg sent a
copy of the same to Captain Inatsuki of the Japanese
Naval Landing Party, who stated that there are no
objections from his point of view, and forwarded a
letter of consent to Dr.Siegelberg.
        The subject of the above play is definitely
political and deals partly with the "Racial Theory".
Scenes in a concentration camp (Act 4) dealing with
atrocities and tortures of Jews are vividly described.
The play which cannot be classified as cultural or
recreational is likely to cause incidents and breach of
peace, if staged publicly and without Police protection.
Attached to this report are several exerts of the play
and their translations.
        Enquiries reveal that Dr.Siegelberg's reason
for staging "The Matrimony of Dr.Brach" in Shanghai is,
of an entirely commercial nature, namely, to assist
the sale of the said play in the U.S.A. To push the
sale of his manuscript Dr.Siegelberg requires enthusiastic
press reviews, which he is able to obtain, being the
chief editor of the "Jewish Chronicle".

        上述剧作的主题具有明确的政治性，部分涉及“种族理论”。剧中第四幕关于集中营的场景，生动描述了针对犹太人的暴行与酷刑。该剧无法被归类为文化或娱乐性质，若在没有警务保护的情况下公开上演，可能会引发事端并破坏治安。本报告附有该剧的部分摘录及其译文。
        经查询获悉，西格尔贝格博士在上海上演《布拉赫博士的婚姻》的原因完全出于商业性质，即为了协助该剧在美国的销售。为了推动其剧本的销售，西格尔贝格博士需要热情的报刊评论，而作为《犹太纪事报》（Jewish Chronicle）的主编，他能够获得此类评论。

To the
Commissioner,
Shanghai Municipal Police.

Sir,

We beg leave to apply for the permission to stage our play,
"Die Ehe des Doktor Brach" (The matrimony of Dr. Brach) in the Kinchow Road
Refugee Jewish Centre (Kinchow Buehne). The play is in the German language.

The above-mentioned play treats a problem, that for years
has occupied the minds of the Jews in Europe: "Racial Theory". Following
are the contents of the play:

Shortly before the German occupation of Austria, Dr. Brach,
a Jewish journalist, is about to be divorced by his wife Christine, an
"Aryan". The reason for the divorce is, that Christine has fallen in love
with another man. When the Germans take over, Dr. Brach is arrested and
taken to a Concentration Camp. This event makes his wife change her mind.
She resolves to give up the divorce and to hold out until her husband will
be freed. She fights untiringly for the release and finally succeeds. In
this fight lasting many months, the couple again gets convinced, that they
belong to one another, so they emigrate together to Shanghai.

The play sets out to prove, that love between two people,
even if they seemingly belong to different races, is stronger than any
"Racial Theory". The play does not decide itself for either race and
centres on the fight of the "Aryan" woman for her Jewish husband.

总监

先生：

我们谨申请获准在锦州路犹太难民中心（锦州剧场）上演我们的剧目《布拉赫医生的婚姻》（"Die Ehe des Doktor Brach"）。该剧使用德语演出。

上述剧目探讨了一个多年来一直萦绕在欧洲犹太人心头的问题：“种族理论”。以下是该剧的内容概要：

在德国占领奥地利前夕，犹太记者布拉赫医生正面临其“雅利安”妻子克里斯蒂娜提出的离婚。离婚的原因是克里斯蒂娜爱上了另一个男人。当德军接管后，布拉赫医生被捕并被送往集中营。这一事件使他的妻子改变了主意。她决定放弃离婚，并坚持等待丈夫获释。她为争取释放而不懈斗争，并最终取得成功。在这场持续数月的斗争中，夫妇二人再次确信彼此属于对方，因此他们一同移居上海。

该剧旨在证明，两个人之间的爱情，即使他们看似属于不同种族，也比任何“种族理论”更为强大。该剧本身并不偏袒任何种族，而是聚焦于一位“雅利安”女性为其犹太丈夫所作的斗争。

page_data.en:
On account of the problem, of universal interest, discussed
in it, the play has already been accepted by the "Oesterreichische
Buehne" in New York, the foremost theatre of German refugees. At the same
time the play is translated into English.
The two play-wrights (one of them for more than twenty
years editor-in-chief of one of the biggest dailies in Austria) desire
that the play, of such interest for Jews, is staged here in a Refugee
theatre. We intend to show the play only before an exclusively Jewish
Refugee audience and not before the general public. Therefore the
"Kinohow-Buehne", the theatre in the Jewish Refugee Centre, Kinohow Road,
has been chosen.
The play being staged in Hongkew, has already been
examined by the Japanese authorities. They have no objections at all and
have forwarded to us their written consent.
Therefore we hope and expect that the Shanghai Municipal
Police will give us the necessary permission.
We remain, Sir,
Your obedient servants
Mark Siegelberg

鉴于剧中讨论的问题具有普遍的关注度，该剧已被纽约的“奥地利舞台”（Oesterreichische Buehne）——即德裔难民中首屈一指的剧院——所接受。同时，该剧正被翻译成英文。

两位剧作家（其中一位曾担任奥地利最大日报之一的总编辑长达二十余年）希望，这部对犹太人而言极具意义的剧目能在一家难民剧院上演。我们计划仅面向纯粹的犹太难民观众演出，而不向公众开放。因此，我们选择了位于虹口路（Kinohow Road）犹太难民中心的“虹口舞台”（Kinohow-Buehne）。

由于该剧将在虹口上演，业经日本当局审查。他们毫无异议，并已将书面同意书转交予我方。

因此，我们希望并期待上海公共租界工部局警务处能给予我们必要的许可。

此致，
敬礼

马克·西格尔伯格
